page: Vultr voc-g-64c-192gb-960s-amd is an x86_64 architecture server within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC processors running at 2.0 GHz, structured as 32 physical cores with hyper-threading. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 100556.13 and a Passmark CPU score of 79514.14, both placing in the top 25%. Single-core performance is also notable, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 10% at 3143.25. Memory performance is highly competitive; the Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10%, supported by a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 340.62 GB/sec. The server demonstrates strong throughput in static web serving at 47.83 GB/sec and handles 87.2 million Redis SET operations per second.

While the server excels in multi-threaded tasks, such as bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 384.83 GB/sec, single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average tier. For AI workloads, the system achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 53.85 tokens/sec on medium (7B) LLM models, though prompt processing for the same model remains average. The 1:3 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation make this server highly suitable for high-concurrency web serving, database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
